transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

Don’t test inside the microwave yourself. A microwave can retain a lethal high-voltage charge in its capacitor even when unplugged, and the components related to the magnetron operate at several thousand volts. Do not plug it in with the cover off or bypass the door switches.

Since the cover is already loose:

1. Unplug it and leave it unplugged.
2. Do not touch the capacitor, transformer, magnetron terminals, wiring, or any metal terminals inside.
3. Refit the cover and all screws before reconnecting power.
4. Arrange service or replace the unit.

Your symptoms—turntable, light, fan, and timer all work, but no heat—usually point to the high-voltage section: magnetron, inverter/HV transformer, diode, capacitor, thermal cutoff, or control board. Those aren’t safe DIY diagnostic items without proper HV safety training and equipment.

Safe checks you can make from outside the unit:
• Confirm it isn’t in Demo Mode (check the Samsung manual/model number; demo mode runs everything except heating).
• Try a different known-working wall outlet; avoid extension leads.
• Check whether it heats at full power with a cup of water for 1 minute—only with the case fully reinstalled. If not, stop using it.

For an older countertop microwave, repair often costs close to or more than replacement; for an over-the-range or built-in Samsung, a qualified appliance technician is usually worthwhile.
